summary.text: 假 is conventionally analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 亻 supplies a person-related meaning and 叚 a sound cue. Another account proposes that 人 was added to distinguish its written form from 叚. Both “false” and “borrow” are recorded, but their order is unresolved.

formation.text: The conventional analysis is phonosemantic: 亻 contributes a person-related meaning and 叚 supplies a sound cue. A competing proposal treats 人 as an addition distinguishing 假 from 叚 in Qin-period writing. The accounts are not reconciled by the cited evidence.

components.text: 亻 is the positional side form of 人. In the conventional analysis it contributes a person-related meaning; another account proposes it was added to distinguish 假 from 叚 in Qin-period writing.
叚 is conventionally analyzed as the phonetic component of 假. Accounts of 叚’s bronze forms and other uses concern that character and do not establish a graphic sequence for 假.

sound.text: In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese notation, 叚 and 假 (the listed “borrow; false” reading) are both reconstructed *Cə.kˤraʔ. This comparison applies to that reading; the same dataset lists a separate reading of 假.

history.text: A scholarly account reports 叚 in excavated pre-Qin texts and 假 in Qin-period documents. It interprets a document dated to 221 BCE as distinguishing lending written with 叚 from borrowing written with 假, and proposes 人 as a differentiating addition. This remains a scholarly interpretation.
Later texts are reported to mix the spellings 叚 and 假. The cited material does not document a detailed sequence of dated graphic changes through later script styles.

Descriptions of 叚 analyze its bronze forms as 爪, 又, and 石, and record uses read as “blessing,” “fault,” interrogative words, and others. These accounts concern 叚, not an established evolutionary path for 假.

uncertainties.text: The conventional analysis assigns 亻 a semantic role and 叚 a phonetic role; another proposal treats 人 as a differentiating addition. Their relationship remains unresolved.
The evidence does not establish a dated development from “borrow” to “false.” A proposed path through “simulate” remains disputed.
The historical sound comparison is available in one reconstruction system, but the cited evidence does not establish that it applies to every reading of 假.

senses.text: 假 is glossed as “not true,” and a cited classical example uses it to mean “false” or “not so.” The first occurrence is not securely dated in the cited material.

senses.period: classical text; composition and attestation dating unresolved
senses.text: A cited classical example uses 假 for borrowing a passage. The Qin-period distinction between lending with 叚 and borrowing with 假 is a scholarly interpretation of a dated document.

senses.period: historical and current; first attestation unresolved
senses.text: Textual examples record temporary or acting uses, and modern definitions include “vacation.” The evidence does not establish when these uses arose or how they relate to “borrow” or “false.”

limitations.text: The cited senses establish neither their relative chronology nor a continuous semantic development. In particular, the proposed path from borrowing through simulation to falsehood remains disputed.

overview.text: 假 conventionally combines a person-related element with 叚 as a sound cue. It means “false” and is also used for “borrow,” but the order of these meanings is unresolved.

components.text: 亻 is the side form of 人 and conventionally contributes a person-related meaning; its proposed role as a differentiating addition is debated.
叚 is conventionally treated as the sound component. The historical sound comparison supports one reading of 假, not every use.

relationships.text: In the conventional analysis of 假, 亻 contributes a person-related meaning; a competing account treats 人 as a differentiating addition.
The conventional analysis assigns 叚 the sound role. One Old Chinese reconstruction lists matching forms for 叚 and a reading of 假; this does not establish the role for every reading.
